# Legal-Eye

> AI contract review for South Africa. Upload a lease, offer to purchase,
> employment contract, suretyship or commercial agreement and get a risk rating
> out of 10, the clauses that need attention, and the South African statutes the
> document actually engages, all in about a minute.

Legal-Eye is built specifically for South African law. It is not a general
contract tool wearing a South African label. Reviews apply the Consumer Protection
Act 68 of 2008, the National Credit Act 34 of 2005, the Alienation of Land Act
68 of 1981, the Electronic Communications and Transactions Act 25 of 2002, the
Companies Act 71 of 2008, the Rental Housing Act 50 of 1999, POPIA, FICA and
others, together with the leading South African judgments on contract, including Beadica
231 CC v Trustees Oregon Trust [2020] ZACC 13, Barkhuizen v Napier [2007] ZACC
5, and the Shifren principle on non-variation clauses.

## What it does

- Reads PDF, DOCX and TXT, including scanned PDFs via OCR, which matters because most signed
  South African agreements are scans.
- Records the document's facts as structured data, then re-derives every number
  in plain code: does the payment schedule reconcile to the stated total, what
  is the real unit price, do quantities agree across the bundle.
- Validates South African identifiers arithmetically: ID numbers by Luhn
  checksum and encoded date of birth, CIPC registration numbers by format, year
  and entity-type suffix, SARS VAT and income tax numbers, and Master's Office
  trust numbers, including whether the Master's Office letter is present. Without
  it, a trust number is not unique.
- Applies only the South African statutes the document engages: the Rental
  Housing Act for a lease, the Alienation of Land Act for a property sale, the
  National Credit Act for a loan, the Diamonds Act for a minerals deal.
- Returns a risk rating from 1 to 10 with a band from Low to Critical, derived
  by a fixed rule from the findings rather than chosen by the model.

## Who it is for

South African businesses, attorneys, conveyancers, paralegals, landlords,
tenants, property buyers, employers and employees who need to understand a
contract before signing or paying against it. Reports can be written for a
legal professional or in plain language.

## Accuracy and citations

South African courts have ordered costs against practitioners personally and
referred them to the Legal Practice Council for filing AI-fabricated legal
authorities. The cautionary cases are Mavundla v MEC: COGTA KZN [2025] ZAKZPHC 2 and Northbound
Processing v SADPMR [2025] ZAGPJHC 661. Legal-Eye therefore may only cite from a
curated, human-checked list of South African statutes and judgments, and every
citation in its output is checked against that list in code before the reader
sees it. Anything outside the list is flagged as unverified rather than
published as fact.

## Privacy

Documents are read in memory and deleted immediately after analysis. Personal
identifiers are replaced with placeholders. That covers South African ID
numbers, email addresses, telephone numbers and account numbers, and they are before any text is sent for
analysis and restored only in the report shown on screen. Analysis is performed
by a third-party AI provider outside South Africa, disclosed as required by
section 18 of the Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013.

## What it is not

Legal-Eye is not a law firm and does not give legal advice. Using it creates no
attorney-client relationship. Under the Legal Practice Act 28 of 2014, only an
admitted legal practitioner may appear in court or prepare documents for use in
legal proceedings. Legal-Eye does neither, and must not be used for court
papers. It is a triage tool: use it to work out what needs an attorney's
attention, then consult one.
